headline: Chicago ferrous scrap up $30/gross ton in October
detail: All grades rose, the first prime-grade increase since February. Tighter scrap flows, better export demand and healthy Midwest mill buying drove it.

headline: Export scrap still flat even as mills pay more
detail: Argus says domestic mill prices rose in October, but export yard prices at major ports didn't move. Weak overseas buying keeps a ceiling on US scrap.

headline: Copper scrap down about 2¢/lb on the week
detail: North American aluminum scrap was broadly lower for Oct 9–15, while brass and zinc scrap edged up and lead held.

headline: Copper bounced Friday after three losing days
detail: Hot US inflation raised the odds of more Fed rate hikes and weighed on demand outlook. Strikes and weather at Chilean mines are limiting the downside.

headline: Palladium at a one-year-plus low; platinum near 3-month low
detail: Palladium is down about 14% in a month and 25% on the year. This feeds straight into catalytic converter values.

headline: Aluminum hit its lowest since February; nickel a 42-week low
detail: Aluminum lost about 7% over four weeks. Nickel stays under pressure from oversupply, with LME stocks near 283,000 tonnes.

headline: US hot-rolled coil near $1,340, up about 65% on the year
detail: Steel stays strong while iron ore sits near four-year lows on heavy supply and full Chinese port stocks.

headline: US new-vehicle sales up 4.4% in September
detail: About 1.32 million vehicles sold, with hybrids strong. August's selling rate was 16.8 million a year, among the best of 2026.

headline: US construction spending up 0.9% in August
detail: Annual rate of $2.20 trillion, but spending is still down 2.9% year to date versus 2025.

headline: China's property support steadies metals demand but doesn't revive it
detail: StoneX says Beijing's measures put a floor under base-metal demand; property sales and investment are still falling.

headline: Section 232 metal tariffs: steel at 50%
detail: The steel, aluminum and copper tariff rules were revised by a June 1 proclamation that took effect June 8. Aluminum scrap is excluded.
